questions.question: Neumann's principle states that …

options.a: the symmetry group of a physical property contains the point group of the crystal
options.b: every tensor component is non-zero unless forbidden by translations
options.c: only polar tensors are affected by crystal symmetry
options.d: magnetic order never changes response tensors

questions.hint: Symmetry of the cause appears in the effect.
questions.explanation: Every response tensor must be invariant under all operations of the (magnetic) point group; components that are not invariant vanish.

questions.question: How does a spin (or magnetic moment) transform?
questions.explanation: S and L are axial (do not flip under inversion) and odd under time reversal.

questions.question: The spin current J^{S_k}_i = {v_i, S_k}/2 is …

options.a: polar in i and k, T-odd
options.b: polar in i, axial in k, T-even
options.c: axial in i, polar in k, T-odd

questions.explanation: v is polar & T-odd, S is axial & T-odd; their product is polar(i)×axial(k) and T-even. Hence D(R)=det(R) R⊗R⊗R for σ^k_ij.

questions.question: A type-II (grey) magnetic space group …

options.b: contains T itself as a symmetry
options.c: contains T only combined with a translation

questions.explanation: Grey groups G1' contain pure time reversal: paramagnets and non-magnetic crystals.

questions.question: Which symmetry forbids ALL macroscopic T-odd responses (anomalous Hall, magnetic SHE, MOKE …)?

options.c: T or T·τ (time reversal, possibly with a translation)

questions.hint: Point-group part of T·τ is the identity combined with T.
questions.explanation: For macroscopic tensors only the point part matters; T or T·τ maps a T-odd tensor onto minus itself.

questions.question: The anomalous Hall effect corresponds to which part of σ_ij?
questions.explanation: Onsager: σ_ij(M)=σ_ji(−M). The part odd in M is antisymmetric; σ^odd_ij = ε_ijk h_k with Hall vector h.

questions.question: In a PT-symmetric antiferromagnet the electronic bands are …
questions.explanation: PT maps (k, ↑) to (k, ↓), so every band is doubly degenerate although T is broken.

questions.question: Which combination characterises an altermagnet?

options.c: compensated, neither PT nor T·τ, non-relativistic spin splitting

questions.explanation: Altermagnets (e.g. RuO2, CrSb, MnTe) are compensated collinear magnets whose sublattices are related by rotations, not by translation or inversion.

questions.question: Which magnetic point group allows an anomalous Hall effect?
questions.hint: Compare the outputs for Pt, RuO2 [001] and Fe [001].
questions.explanation: 4/mm'm' (bcc Fe, m∥z) allows σ_xy^odd; m-3m1' is grey and 4'/mmm' (RuO2, Néel∥z) forbids the Hall vector.

questions.question: Hands-on: what is the magnetic point group of monoclinic MoO2 (examples/vasp/MoO2_monoclinic)?
questions.explanation: MoO2 is non-magnetic: grey group P2_1/c1' (BNS 14.76), magnetic point group 2/m1'.

questions.question: Hands-on: what is the BNS symbol of the magnetic space group of examples/vasp/bcc_Fe_m001 (m ∥ z)?
questions.explanation: I4/mm'm' (BNS 139.537): the 4-fold axis is along m; mirrors containing m are primed.

questions.question: Hands-on: for bcc Fe with m ∥ z, the anomalous Hall vector h points along …
questions.explanation: h = (0, 0, σ_xy): the Hall vector is parallel to the magnetisation, as for any ferromagnet with a high-symmetry moment.

questions.question: Hands-on: how many independent T-odd (magnetic) spin-conductivity components does bcc Fe (m ∥ z) have?
questions.explanation: σ^x_xz, σ^x_zx, σ^z_xx and σ^z_zz (plus symmetry-related ones): spin-polarised longitudinal/transverse currents with spin ∥ m.

questions.question: Hands-on: RuO2 with Néel vector ∥ [001]. Is the anomalous Hall effect allowed?
questions.explanation: P4_2'/mnm' (MPG 4'/mmm') forbids any Hall vector: no axial vector is invariant under all its operations.

questions.question: Hands-on: RuO2 with Néel ∥ [001]: what is the form of the T-odd σ^z block?
questions.explanation: The symmetric, T-odd σ^z_xy=σ^z_yx is the spin-splitter effect of altermagnetic RuO2 (spin current with spin ∥ Néel vector).

questions.question: Hands-on: BNS symbol of RuO2 with the Néel vector along [100] (examples/vasp/RuO2_Neel100_SOC)?
questions.explanation: Pnn'm' (58.398), MPG mm'm': rotating the Néel vector into the plane lowers the symmetry.

questions.question: Hands-on: for RuO2 with Néel ∥ [100], the Hall vector is along …
questions.explanation: h = (0, −σ_xz, 0): the crystal Hall vector is perpendicular to the Néel vector — a hallmark of the crystal Hall effect.

questions.question: Hands-on: how many independent T-even spin Hall components does monoclinic MoO2 have?
questions.explanation: 13 (cubic Pt has 1). The orbital Hall tensor has the same 13 components; without SOC all spin components vanish but the orbital ones survive.

questions.question: MoO2 has point group 2/m with unique axis y. Which spin/orbital conductivity components σ^k_ij can be non-zero?

options.a: only those with k ⊥ i ⊥ j
options.b: those with an odd number of y indices among (k, i, j)
options.c: those with an even number of y indices

questions.hint: C2y maps x → −x, z → −z; the tensor is axial (det R = +1 for C2).
questions.explanation: Under C2y a component picks (−1)^(n_x+n_z); invariance needs n_x+n_z even, i.e. n_y odd. Inversion adds nothing for an axial rank-3 tensor. Examples: σ^y_xx, σ^y_yy, σ^x_xy (unconventional) and σ^z_xy (conventional).

questions.question: SymPhase analyses a calculation WITHOUT spin–orbit coupling. Which statement is right?

options.b: the true symmetry is a larger spin group, so some components allowed by the magnetic group may vanish without SOC
options.c: no magnetic group can be defined

questions.explanation: Without SOC spin rotations are decoupled from the lattice (spin groups); the relativistic MSG analysis gives the components that SOC can switch on.
